headline: Protein language models repurposed for disorder, binding site, and enzyme prediction
label: Protein Language Model Prediction
summary: Recent work adapts pretrained protein language model embeddings to specific tasks while addressing pooling and evaluation bias.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the reuse of pretrained protein language model representations for task-specific prediction. UdonPred uses ProstT5 embeddings in a lightweight network to predict per-residue disorder, and Seq2Pocket finetunes a protein language model with an augmented sc-PDB training set and structure-aware post-processing for spatially consistent binding site prediction. HIT-EC applies evidential deep learning within a hierarchical interpretable transformer to predict enzyme commission numbers from sequence. Other items extend the scope differently: ExoShorkie applies transfer learning to predict RNA-seq coverage on exogenous yeast genomes, DynaPIN extracts dynamic interface fingerprints from MD simulations, and the exon-exon interaction study examines both the power and limits of structure-based prediction. What is new in this set is attention to evaluation control, as the kcat study proposes a bias-aware pairwise formulation to recover true mutation effects from biased mutant datasets.
